questions.title: Sum with a for loop
questions.prompt:
Write a `for` loop from scratch that adds the whole numbers **1 through 10** together.

- Store the running sum in a variable named `total` (declare it yourself).
- After the loop, write `total` to the console with `console.log()`.

Do not use arrays or any built-in math helpers — just the loop.
hints: A for loop has three parts: for (initialization; condition; increment) { ... }
Start total at 0 before the loop, then use total += i inside it.

questions.title: Loop through an array of scores
questions.prompt:
The starter code declares an array of test scores. Using a loop (`for`, `for...of`, or `while`):

1. Find the highest score and store it in a variable named `highest`. **Do not** use `Math.max()` or `sort()`.
2. Count how many scores are **80 or higher** and store the count in a variable named `passing`.
hints: Start highest at the first element (scores[0]) and passing at 0.
Inside the loop, use an if statement for each job: one compares to highest, one compares to 80.

tests.name: Does not use Math.max() or sort()

questions.title: Write a function that returns initials
questions.prompt:
Write a function named `getInitials` that accepts one parameter, a person's full name, and **returns** their initials as an uppercase string.

Examples:

```
getInitials("Grace Hopper")          // "GH"
getInitials("ada king lovelace")     // "AKL"
getInitials("  Alan   Turing ")      // "AT"
```

Notice the last example: extra spaces must be ignored. You may write it as a function declaration, a function expression, or an arrow function.
hints: trim() removes leading and trailing spaces; split(" ") breaks a string into an array of words.
Splitting "Alan   Turing" on a single space gives empty strings — skip any word whose length is 0.
word.charAt(0) or word[0] gets the first letter; toUpperCase() converts it.

questions.title: One line to change a heading
questions.prompt:
The page below has a heading that still says **Loading...**.

Write **exactly one statement** of plain JavaScript (no jQuery) that changes the heading's text to:

```
Welcome to the Exam
```

Select the heading by its `id`.

tests.name: Heading text is "Welcome to the Exam"
Answer is a single statement
tests.code:
const lines = code.split("\n").map(l => l.trim()).filter(l => l && !l.startsWith("//"));
return lines.length === 1 && lines[0].replace(/;\s*$/, "").indexOf(";") === -1;

questions.prompt:

- Select **only** the `<li>` elements inside the list whose id is `task_list`.
- Loop through them and add the CSS class `highlight` to each one.

The CSS rule for `.highlight` is already in the page's style sheet. The items in `#done_list` must **not** be changed.

questions.title: Click counter with an event handler
questions.prompt:
The page has a button and a `<span>` that shows `0`.

Write plain JavaScript so that **each time the button is clicked**, the number in the span goes up by one (1, 2, 3, ...).

- Attach the handler with `addEventListener()` (or the `onclick` property).
- Wrap your code so it runs after the DOM is loaded, the way the book does with the `DOMContentLoaded` event.
hints: document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => { ... }); runs code once the page is ready.
Read the span with textContent, convert it with parseInt() or Number(), add 1, and write it back.
Or keep the count in a variable that lives outside the click handler.

tests.name: Span still shows 0 before any click
Shows 3 after two more clicks

questions.title: Image swap with links
questions.prompt:
This is the classic image-swap application. Each thumbnail link's `href` points to a larger image.

Write plain JavaScript so that when the user clicks any link inside `#image_links`:

1. The `src` of the image `#main_image` changes to the clicked link's `href`.
2. The caption `#caption` changes to the link's `title` attribute.
3. The browser does **not** follow the link (cancel the default action).

setup.html:
Color Gallery

  • Red
  • Green
  • Blue

Red

hints: document.querySelectorAll("#image_links a") gets every link; loop and add a click handler to each.
Inside the handler, evt.currentTarget (or this, in a regular function) is the clicked link. Use its href and title.
Call evt.preventDefault() to stop the browser from following the link.

tests.name: Clicking "Green" swaps the image src
Clicking "Blue" updates the caption
The link's default action is cancelled

questions.title: One jQuery statement to hide elements
questions.prompt:
jQuery is loaded on this page.

Write **one jQuery statement** that hides every element with the class `answer` that is **inside** the element with id `faqs`.

The paragraph with class `answer` in the footer must stay visible.

setup.html:
What is jQuery?

A JavaScript library that makes DOM scripting easier.

Why use it?

It handles cross-browser differences for you.

Footer note: this one should stay visible.

hints: jQuery selectors use CSS syntax: a descendant selector is "#parent .child".
The hide() method sets display to none.

questions.title: FAQ toggle with a jQuery effect
questions.prompt:
jQuery is loaded. Each answer `<div>` starts hidden by the CSS.

Write jQuery code so that when the user clicks any `<h2>` inside `#faqs`:

1. The class `minus` is toggled on the clicked `<h2>` (the CSS uses it to change the + to a −).
2. The `<div>` **right after** that `<h2>` slides down if hidden, or up if visible, using a jQuery effect.

Use the ready event handler, as in the book.

setup.html:
What is a closure?

A function together with the variables it remembers from its outer scope.

What does $ mean in jQuery?

It's a short name for the jQuery() function.

hints: $("#faqs h2").click(function() { ... }) — inside a regular function, $(this) is the clicked heading.
toggleClass("minus") adds the class if missing and removes it if present.
next() gets the next sibling; slideToggle() animates it up or down.

tests.name: Clicking the first heading adds class "minus"
The first answer is shown after the animation
The second answer is still hidden
Clicking again removes "minus" and hides the answer

questions.title: Validate a form before it submits
questions.prompt:
jQuery is loaded. Write a **submit** event handler for the form `#email_form` that validates the email field:

- If `#email` is empty (after trimming spaces) **or** does not contain an `@`, put the text `Enter a valid email.` in the `<span>` right after the field, and **stop the form from submitting**.
- Otherwise, clear the span (set it to an empty string) and let the form submit.
hints: $("#email_form").submit( evt => { ... }) attaches a submit handler.
val() gets the field value; trim() removes spaces; indexOf("@") returns -1 when there is no @.
evt.preventDefault() stops the submission. $("#email").next() is the span.

tests.name: Empty email shows the error message
Empty email cancels the submit
Email without @ is rejected
Valid email clears the message and submits
